correctness.rationale: For H not identity, any orbit of a moved-row vertex would use the same column twice, impossible in a face; invariant supports thus use only pointwise-fixed rows, giving exact geometric fixed locus. Pure shellability follows from m≥m−4+2k, and a complete face count computes the sphere multiplicities. For torsion, Theorem 5.7 of arxiv:2610.37827 provides the integral cyclic group and relations; exchanging row 2/3 maps q2 to q3=−q2, and full-column exterior orientation gives sign(sigma). One-dimensionality and conjugacy extend row action to all S4. Direct mod3 and mod2 chain checks and quotient-presentation computations corroborate critical finite cases; no finite computation is used to justify the universal quantifier.

value.rationale: The natural infinite torsion-bearing family yields contrasting equivariant data: a nontrivial integral sign module in ambient homology versus torsion-free, precisely enumerated fixed-point wedges for every nontrivial row subgroup. These are invariants relevant to equivariant topology and obstruction methods that are neither determined by ambient Betti numbers nor by a bare torsion-existence claim. Full subgroup and all-parameter coverage, rather than an arbitrary finite slice, motivates the classification.
